workingTitle: A dead star is circled by two separate rings of planetary wreckage
freshness: Peer-reviewed open-access Nature Astronomy article published October 26, 2026; selected within the preferred 15-day window.
coreFacts: VLT/X-shooter spectra of white dwarf WD J1328-1450 show quadruple-peaked calcium and oxygen emission lines, unlike the double-peaked profiles of all 21 previously known gaseous white-dwarf debris discs.
The line velocities map to two separated gaseous rings extending from 0.14 to 0.34 solar radii and from 0.54 to 1.93 solar radii.
Repeated observations from 2021 to 2023 show that the two-ring structure remained stable for more than two years.
The inner ring contains magnesium emission while the outer ring is strongly magnesium-depleted, suggesting debris with different compositions.

The authors infer that two surviving planetary bodies probably generate and confine the gas, but neither body has been directly detected and exact sizes depend on orbit, density, and internal strength.
caveats: The two planetary bodies are inferred from the stable separated gas rings and are not directly observed.
The outer body's possible Pluto-to-Moon scale is an upper limit that depends on its location, density, and internal strength.
Different ring compositions could reflect two parent bodies or different layers of one differentiated body.
